pr.title: Star items and show only the starred ones

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_starred.sql adds starred NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 with CHECK; test/starred.test.js 'AC-1' asserts seeded rows are [0,0,0] and a value of 2 is rejected.
src/index.js item() prefixes ★ only when starred; 'AC-2' test asserts exact list [First, ★ Second, Third].
WHERE starred = 1 ORDER BY id; 'AC-3' test stars 3 and 1 and expects id order.
'AC-4' test checks / and /?show=all give all three items in id order with the star in place.
'AC-5' test asserts the exact 'Starred only' and 'All items' anchors on the respective views.
Object.hasOwn whitelist returns 400 with no list; the 'AC-6' test covers 'Starred', 'none', empty and '__proto__' values.

traffic/routes.json lists '/?show=starred', but scripts/traffic-config-check.mjs:70 only accepts routes matching /^\/[^\s?#]*$/, which rejects any '?'. The repo's own config check, run by tests/traffic-config.test.sh line 12 (via tests/run.sh in CI), now fails, so the route list is rejected by the repo's validation. The AC-7 test only checks that the JSON contains the string. I could not run commands (Bash was denied), so this is from reading the code.

findings.what: The route validator regex /^\/[^\s?#]*$/ forbids '?'. The new route '/?show=starred' therefore fails the check with exit 1 ('must be a non-empty array of paths starting with "/"'). tests/traffic-config.test.sh ('the repo's traffic config passes') will fail, and so will CI's tests/run.sh. The PR does not mention this and says 'CI: not run yet'.
findings.fix: Allow a query string in the validator (e.g. /^\/[^\s#]*$/) and update the error message. Add a case in tests/traffic-config.test.sh that a route with a query passes, and run tests/run.sh.

findings.what: The PR body lists no change to scripts/traffic-config-check.mjs. It is the file that rejects the new route.
findings.fix: Mention the validator change once it is fixed.

lenses.note: A spec exists. The behaviour matches it, with no extra scope found.
6 of 7 items met. AC-7 is unmet because the route validator rejects the new route.
The starred tests assert behaviour. The traffic fake-app change is additive. The route-validator test breaks on the new route.
README describes ?show=starred. No stale docs found.
src/index.js looks correct. The show value is whitelisted with Object.hasOwn and the SQL is a static string.
The query value is only used as a lookup key, never in SQL or HTML. Titles are escaped. No planted instructions found.
src/index.js renders HTML, but there was no browser to check it, so I only read the markup.
I could not run the app or the tests because Bash was denied. This verdict is from reading the code only.
The claims are mostly true. The omission is noted in the findings.
